behaviour_changes: Ternary in-bounds now refuses: on v300, ternary a = c ? k : p with a[0] worked correctly (11 for c=1, 77 for c=0); on v301, ANY ternary kosh assignment refuses at compile time (E_KOSH_DVARA, maybe-kosh), even for in-bounds reads that were correct. Safe (no silent over-read possible) but rejects valid programs that used ternary kosh values in-bounds. Design is coherent (definite-kosh sources like call results are tracked and bounds-checked; maybe-kosh sources like ternary are refused), but the breakage should be a conscious owner decision, not a silent side effect.

Mala -> kosh assignment now refuses at compile time, not runtime: on v300, a = m; a = k; a[100] runtime-refused (assignment marked it as kosh, so out-of-bounds read refused); on v301, it compile-refuses (E_VITTI_PRAKAR, type-fixed). Same outcome (refusal, not silent/crash), just earlier (compile time instead of runtime) - stricter, not a regression.

bypasses.global_inbounds: holder = k; holder[0] (in-bounds) -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'k' in global vitti, at the assignment). Fix is 'refuse kosh-to-global assignment entirely' (not 'track and bounds-check') - so even valid in-bounds global kosh reads refuse on v301 (they worked on v300 in-bounds). Safe, but a breaking change for valid uses, like ternary in-bounds - owner's decision.
bypasses.global_koshcell: outer[0] = inner; holder = outer[0]; holder[100] -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'inner' in cell/region/memory, at the outer[0] = inner store itself). Same (at the cell store, O3 fix).
bypasses.global_malacell: m[0] = k; holder = m[0]; holder[100] -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'k' in cell/region/memory, at the m[0] = k store itself). Refused even earlier (at the cell store, O2 fix), so the global assignment is never reached.
bypasses.global_ternary: holder = c ? k : p; holder[0] (in-bounds) -> E_KOSH_DVARA (maybe-kosh, at the ternary assignment). Refused even for in-bounds reads (ternary to global refused, same as ternary to local).
bypasses.global_via_call: holder = make_kosh() (call result); holder[100] -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh '' in global vitti). Refuses (no bypass). Cosmetic nit: error shows an empty kosh name (kosh '') because the kosh comes from a call result, not a named variable - refusal holds, but diagnostic should name the function or the result instead of an empty string.
bypasses.mala_after_kosh: holder = k; holder = m; holder[100] -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'k' in global vitti, at the kosh assignment). Kosh assignment refused first, so mala reassignment never matters (cannot clear a check that already refused the program).
bypasses.mala_then_kosh: holder = m; holder = k; holder[100] -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'k' in global vitti, at the kosh assignment). Global-door check fires before the type-fixed check (which would have been E_VITTI_PRAKAR for the type change) - kosh-to-global is refused regardless of the global's prior type.
bypasses.two_functions: set_a() assigns holder = k; set_b() assigns holder = k2; read in mukhya -> E_KOSH_DVARA (kosh 'k' in global vitti, at the first assignment). First assignment already refuses, so the program never compiles; second assignment moot.
